text:
alex: Heads-up — I pushed a terraform change that creates the payments namespace and a service account for the billing job. After the deploy the job started failing with AWS permission errors (STS:AssumeRole). Anyone seen this pattern?

maya: Yep — usually means the IRSA annotation (eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn) ended up on the pod or deployment instead of the serviceAccount resource. Can you paste the k8s manifest or the terraform snippet you used? :thinking_face: 

alex: I used the k8s manifest via `kubernetes_manifest` in TF. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/changes/4523 — snippet I applied: 
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: payments-sa
  namespace: payments
# annotations missing here in my file
```

sam: The aws-iam-authenticator expects the annotation on the service account itself. If you used Helm values to set `serviceAccount.annotations` that should work, but if the chart creates its own SA after TF runs the timing can be off. Did you create the SA via TF and also let helm create it?

alex: Ah — the helm chart is still creating the SA. I added a `kubernetes_manifest` for payments-sa earlier thinking it would override. Deploy-bot shows both resources were created.

deploy-bot: apply finished for infra/cluster/payments (plan #78) — created: kubernetes_namespace.payments, kubernetes_manifest.payments-sa, helm_release/payments-job

maya: That explains it. Two options: 1) Have Helm manage the SA and add `serviceAccount.annotations` in the Helm values so it gets the eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn. 2) Create the SA via TF and set `set serviceAccount.create=false` in Helm so chart reuses your SA. Whichever you pick, ensure the annotation is on the SA: 
```yaml
metadata:
  name: payments-sa
  namespace: payments
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/rdw-payments-role
```

sam: Also verify the OIDC provider mapping exists and that the IAM role has the correct trust policy for the service account namespace/name. Quick command to check SA annotation: `kubectl get sa payments-sa -n payments -o yaml`

alex: For a hotfix I patched the SA with the annotation and the job started succeeding immediately. `kubectl annotate sa payments-sa -n payments eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn=arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/rdw-payments-role --overwrite`

maya: Nice. For the TF change: if you want TF to own the SA, use `kubernetes_service_account` resource and include the annotation in `metadata.0.annotations`. If you prefer Helm manage it, remove the TF SA resource and set `values.serviceAccount.create=false` + `values.serviceAccount.annotations` in the helm_release.

alex: Will revert my create of the SA in TF and add the annotation into the Helm values in the PR. One more question: does anyone know if our common helm values schema uses `serviceAccount.annotations` or `serviceAccountAnnotations`? I can’t remember.

sam: It's `serviceAccount.annotations` for the payments chart (see charts/payments/values.schema.json).

maya: Also add a short note in the PR about why we prefer letting Helm own the SA (chart handles imagePullSecrets and lifecycle). Saves surprises. :+1:

alex: Cool — updating PR now. Thanks all!

sam: Optional follow-up: we should add a CI check that flags double-created SAs in the same namespace. Might save time in future.

maya: Agree. Filing a tiny ticket after this: INFRA-912.

alex: Filed INFRA-912 and linked into the PR. Closing after merge. :)
